findings.title: Detach asynchronous writes from request cancellation
findings.body: The legacy goroutines derive their timeout contexts from the incoming request context. An HTTP request context is canceled when the handler returns, so returning after the unified write cancels the legacy operation rather than allowing it ten seconds to complete. This affects Create, Update, Delete and DeleteCollection and can leave the fallback store missing successful writes. Preserve context values with a cancellation-detached context before applying the timeout.

findings.title: Mirror the committed update instead of reapplying the original updater
findings.body: Legacy.Update now receives the original UpdatedObjectInfo instead of the wrapper containing the unified store's committed result. UpdatedObjectInfo can compute a patch or server-side apply against the old object supplied by each store; applying it again against a stale legacy object can produce a different document or fail validation. The previous implementation explicitly mirrored the committed object. Restore that behavior so the backup receives the actual successful unified update.

findings.title: Preserve write ordering in the legacy mirror
findings.body: Each successful write launches an independent goroutine with no ordering mechanism. Even sequential client requests can therefore be applied in reverse order to legacy storage: a delete can execute before an earlier create, leaving the deleted object recreated, or an older update can overwrite a newer update. A per-resource ordered replication mechanism is needed for the legacy store to remain a usable fallback.

findings.title: Do not label delete metrics with object names
findings.body: The successful Delete path passes name as the kind argument to recordStorageDuration, while the other paths use options.Kind. This creates a distinct metric label value for every deleted resource name, causing unbounded Prometheus series cardinality and incorrectly grouping delete durations. Pass the resource kind instead.

findings.title: Attribute operation metrics to the store actually called
findings.body: DeleteCollection records the asynchronous legacy call through recordStorageDuration, so unified-storage metrics include legacy latency and failures and legacy metrics omit this operation. Similarly, the Create and Update unified failure paths call recordLegacyDuration even though legacy was never invoked. Correct these recorder selections so monitoring can distinguish unified failures from fallback failures.
